review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked its definitions for competition with Mathlib concepts. The definitions are finPart, realGL, archC0, dC0, Dset, pinsQ, W1, FIB, ray, Jm, Laws, Sheet, Wit, Afun, Bfun, Concl and Lm. Almost all of them are specific to the project's adelic and Whittaker setting. They are built from project definitions such as AdelicGL2, archW and whittakerCoefficient. They are not general Mathlib concepts, and I found no Mathlib counterpart for any of them.

The only near-match is `Jm` (line 246). It is the matrix diag(-1,1), which is the underlying matrix of Mathlib's `UpperHalfPlane.J : GL (Fin 2) ℝ`. Mathlib has `val_J : J.val = !![-1, 0; 0, 1]` (MoebiusAction.lean, line 388). The file also proves its own `coe_UpperHalfPlane_J_eq_diagonal`. `Jm` is a Matrix-typed abbreviation, not a GL element. It is used with `Matrix.diagonal`, `Matrix.mul` and `det` lemmas, and it is defeq to the coerced J. I judged this a deliberate named matrix-level abbreviation with a modest conversion cost. It is not a competing independent concept, and the practical case for consolidating is unclear, so I did not report it.

The remaining candidates are standalone theorems (`rat_isReal`, `exists_sq_eq`, `bdd_nat`, `eq_of_glArch_eq_of_glFin_eq'`), which the rubric excludes. I did not check every project-internal definition against the project's own earlier files, only against Mathlib.
